description: This course covers foundational and advanced concepts in software testing, including test planning, test case design, and test execution using industry standards such as ISO/IEC 25010 and IEEE 829. Topics include black-box testing techniques like equivalence partitioning, boundary value analysis, and decision table testing; white-box testing methods such as control flow and data flow analysis; automated testing tools like Selenium and JUnit; test automation frameworks including TestNG and Cucumber; defect management systems like JIRA; and performance testing with JMeter. The course also explores software quality assurance (SQA) practices, test management methodologies like Agile and Waterfall, and the role of software testing in DevOps pipelines. Students will learn to apply testing principles to real-world scenarios using these technologies and methods.

clos.text: Define test case design techniques such as equivalence partitioning and boundary value analysis.
Describe the components of a test plan according to IEEE 829 standards.
Explain the principles of automated testing using Selenium and JUnit.
Apply test automation frameworks like TestNG and Cucumber to real-world software projects.
Evaluate the effectiveness of defect management systems such as JIRA in software testing workflows.
